0000.png.text: Secrets give Devin the passwords, API keys and site cookies it needs, without pasting them into chat.

0001.png.text: To add one, open Settings → Secrets, where your organization and personal secrets live.
0001.png.say: To add one, open Settings, then Secrets, where your organization and personal secrets live.

chunks.text: To add one, open Settings → Secrets, where your organization and personal secrets live.

0008.png.text: Any secret can be referenced by its name, with a dollar sign in front.

chunks.text: Any secret can be referenced by its name,
with a dollar sign in front.

0009.png.text: Organization secrets are shared with your whole team. Personal secrets only work in sessions you start.

chunks.text: Organization secrets are shared with your whole team.
Personal secrets only work in sessions you start.

0010.png.text: Click Add secret, and set the scope to Personal, so only your sessions can use it.

chunks.text: Click Add secret,
and set the scope to Personal,
so only your sessions can use it.

0016.png.text: Then pick a type: a raw secret, a cookie, or a one-time password for two-factor sign-in.

chunks.text: Then pick a type:
a raw secret,
a cookie, or a one-time password for two-factor sign-in.

0019.png.text: A raw secret holds one value, like an API key. Give it a name, the value, and a note so Devin knows when to use it.

chunks.text: A raw secret holds one value,

Give it a name,
the value, and a note so Devin knows

0040.png.text: Secrets are encrypted, and Redact value is on by default, so the value stays hidden in the dashboard.

chunks.text: Secrets are encrypted,

0044.png.text: The new secret shows up under Personal, with its note, and never its value.

0045.png.text: Site cookies keep Devin signed in to web apps. Add another secret, and this time choose Cookie.

chunks.text: Site cookies keep Devin signed in to web

0052.png.text: Name it, then paste the cookies you exported from your browser, as JSON or base64.

0063.png.text: The form parses each cookie, and encodes it for you.

0067.png.text: Now both are ready in any new session you start. Devin types the values straight into the browser, and binds them as environment variables for the commands that need them.
